newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude holds slim gains in rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude holds slim gains in rangebound trade.

text.p: NYMEX crude held onto slim gains Thursday in listless rangebound late trade after the United Nations retained sanctions against Iraq.

"It was expected, so it's not big news. But, we are sustaining gains even though we are overbought by some indicators, so that is a positive sign," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products at Paribas Futures Inc.

At 1417 EDT, June crude was up five cents at $20.26 a barrel. The 5-3-3 stochastics on the spot crude continuation chart indicates prompt crude is overbought, but June crude held technical support early at $20.06.
The U.N. Security Council on Thursday maintained the tough economic sanctions imposed on Baghdad since its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait, diplomats said.
The decision was expected and followed a critical report three weeks ago by the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM), which oversees Iraqi disarmament.

The sanctions include a ban on regular Iraqi oil sales; however, through special arrangment the U.N. has allowed Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months on a renewable basis. June gasoline was up 0.79 cent a gallon at 63.20 cents.
June heating oil was up 0.38 cent at 55.30 cents a gallon.
Dealers noted continued front month spread buying in the June/July heat spread after a sharp rise in the May/June spread prior to May's expiration on Wednesday.
Traders were betting the sizable rollover gap between June and May heat of 3.15 cents would be closed, implying June would strengthen in relation to July.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
